samples.summary: `files download` can now emit a nonsensical `HTTP 200` error message
samples.evidence: The guard is `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes)`. When the request succeeded (ok=true, status 200) but the body carried no bytes, `upstreamErrorJson({status:200, data:undefined})` produces `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR', message:'HTTP 200'}}`. `upstreamMessage` unconditionally prefixes `HTTP ${res.status}` with no check that the status is actually a failure, so an agent is told the failure was "HTTP 200". Before the change the same path printed `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'}}` with no misleading message.

samples.summary: `clampUpstreamText` silently discards any legitimate upstream message that starts with `<`
samples.evidence: `if (!trimmed || trimmed.startsWith('<')) return null;` treats *any* leading `<` as an HTML document. A real backend/class-validator message such as "<html> tags are not allowed in markdown" or "<unknown> field required" is dropped entirely; on the envelope path `safeEnvelope` then substitutes `HTTP ${status}` (line 165), so the upstream's only actionable text is lost while the envelope still claims a real code. Same for a non-string `message` (e.g. a number), which becomes `''` -> null.

samples.summary: `MAX_UPSTREAM_BODY` bound is measured on compact JSON but the output is pretty-printed, so the real stderr bound is several times larger
samples.evidence: `JSON.stringify(whole).length <= MAX_UPSTREAM_BODY` measures the compact form, while both `forwardUpstreamError` (line 225) and `upstreamErrorJson` (line 250) emit `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)`. With indentation and newlines a body that measures 4000 compact can print well over 10 KB — the documented intent ("a stack trace or a megabyte of debug context is not" kept) is only loosely enforced; sibling fields up to ~4 KB each still reach stderr unclamped since only `error.message`/`error.code` are individually capped.

samples.summary: `safeEnvelope` invents a `message` field that the upstream never sent, but only on the oversized branch
samples.evidence: For a small envelope with no `message` key, `'message' in body.error` is false so the output has `{error:{code}}` with no message. For the same envelope carrying a large sibling field, the fallback `{ error: { code, message: error.message ?? `HTTP ${status}` } }` synthesizes `message: 'HTTP <status>'`. The same upstream error therefore yields two different shapes/messages depending only on the size of an unrelated sibling field, which is exactly the shape-instability the change set out to remove.

samples.summary: The claim that "every command that talks to the backend" reports the documented envelope is not true of `login`
samples.evidence: formatter.ts:203-208 asserts every command routes its `!res.ok` branch through `forwardUpstreamError`. `login.ts:62`, `:79` and `:96` still print bare prose to stderr (`'Token exchange failed. Try again...'`, `Failed to fetch workspaces (HTTP ${wsRes.status})`) and call `process.exit(1)`, so an agent parsing stderr as JSON gets nothing parseable from the one command most likely to fail on an expired session. Pre-existing, but the new doc comment and README/error-matrix now state the opposite.

samples.summary: `UpstreamHttpError` is exported but imported nowhere (not even by the new test)
samples.evidence: grep for `UpstreamHttpError` across packages/ matches only its declaration and the throw site in formatter.ts. Nothing consumes the exported class or its `status` field, so the export is dead surface (and the knip lane flags unused exports).

finding.summary: `api-keys` commands bypass `send()`, so the SESSION_EXPIRED/refresh invariant this delta asserts does not hold for them
finding.evidence: The delta routes `api-keys create/list/revoke` (api-keys.ts:22,36,50) through `forwardUpstreamError`, and the new comment in formatter.ts:153-158 plus the new test cases (upstream-error.test.ts:242-244) assert the invariant "every command that talks to the backend" reports the same code, "the client's own 401 SESSION_EXPIRED most of all". But `listApiKeys` (http-client.ts:365-371), `createApiKey` (372-382) and `revokeApiKey` (383-389) call `fetch` directly instead of `this.send(...)`: they never attempt `refreshSession()` on a 401 and never synthesize `sessionExpiredBody()`. Under JWT auth an expired access token on these three commands (a) is not retried after a refresh that would have succeeded — the command fails where every other command succeeds — and (b) surfaces the raw server 401 body, which `forwardUpstreamError` reports as `HTTP_ERROR`, not `SESSION_EXPIRED`. The code an agent branches on therefore still depends on which subcommand it ran, which is exactly the bug this change claims to close; the new tests do not catch it because the fetch stub never exercises the 401/refresh path.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim -- that listApiKeys, createApiKey and revokeApiKey call fetch directly instead of this.send(...), so they never refresh on 401 nor synthesize sessionExpiredBody() -- is false in this working tree. All three methods delegate to requestUrl (http-client.ts:388, 391, 394-397), which calls this.send(...) and returns this.sessionExpiredBody<T>() with status 401 when the refresh fails (http-client.ts:182-193). send (133-154) implements the 401 -> refreshSession() -> single retry with rebuilt auth headers. An exhaustive grep for 'fetch(' in the file yields only three sites -- refreshSession (94) and the two inside send (137, 148) -- so no direct fetch exists in the api-keys path. The cited line range (365-389) actually holds setCell/deleteCell/batchCells, not the api-keys methods. The in-file comments at 166-176 and 380-382 explicitly describe the direct-fetch behavior as the prior state that was removed. Consequently forwardUpstreamError in api-keys.ts:22, 36, 50 receives the SESSION_EXPIRED envelope and forwards that code via safeEnvelope (formatter.ts:158-171), so the asserted invariant does hold. The residual test-coverage concern is outside the Correctness lane and does not establish a production defect.
